added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(0<h<H\leq1\) such that \(H^{-1}\) and \(H/h\) are positive integers and each macro cube of side \(H\) contains at least four fine cubes of side \(h\).  Fix bounded smooth functions \((B_j)\) and \((G_Q)\) with bounded overlap such that \(G_Q=\sum_{j\subset Q}B_j^2\), \(0\leq G_Q\leq1\), and, for a constant \(C_b\) depending only on the fixed bump shapes and \(d\),
\[
 \left[\sum_j a_jB_j\right]_s\leq C_bh^{-s}\max_j|a_j|,
 \;
 \left[\sum_Q z_QG_Q\right]_s\leq C_bH^{-s}\max_Q|z_Q|
 \tag{1}
\]
for \(s\in\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma\}\), together with the analogous supremum bounds.  Assume that every fine cube contains a core of volume at least \(c_bh^d\) on which only its own bump is active and is bounded below by \(c_b>0\), and that each \(G_Q\) is a translated and rescaled copy of one nonconstant macro bump \(g\).  Let the macro signs \((\sigma_Q)\) be independent Rademacher variables.  For each fine coordinate \(j\subset Q\), put \(U_j=q_e\varepsilon_j\), \(V_j=q_b\eta_j\), where \(q_e,q_b>0\), \(0<\delta\leq q_eq_b\), and \(\vartheta=\delta/(q_eq_b)\).  Conditional on the macro signs, take the fine pairs independently with
\[
 \mathbb P_1(\varepsilon_j=a,\eta_j=b)=\frac14,
 \;
 \mathbb P_0(\varepsilon_j=a,\eta_j=b\mid\sigma_Q)
 =\frac14\{1+\vartheta\sigma_Qab\},; a,b\in\{-1,1\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Writing \(u=\sum_jU_jB_j\), \(v=\sum_jV_jB_j\), and \(G=\sum_Q\sigma_QG_Q\), define every null component by
\[
 e_0=\frac12+u,; m_{0,0}=\frac38+v,; \tau_0\equiv\frac18,
 \tag{3}
\]
and every alternative component by
\[
 e_1=\frac12+u,; m_{0,1}=\frac38+v-2\delta G,;
 \tau_1=\frac18+4\delta G.
 \tag{4}
\]
Impose the construction-side inequalities
\[
 C_bq_eh^{-\alpha}\leq L,;
 C_b\{q_bh^{-\beta}+2\delta H^{-\beta}\}\leq L,;
 4C_b\delta H^{-\gamma}\leq L,;
 q_e\leq\frac14,; q_b+2\delta\leq\frac18.
 \tag{5}
\]
Then all four masses in (2) are nonnegative, all coordinate means vanish, \(U_j^2=q_e^2\), \(V_j^2=q_b^2\), and
\[
 \mathbb E_0(U_jV_j\mid\sigma_Q)-\mathbb E_1(U_jV_j)
 =\delta\sigma_Q.
 \tag{6}
\]
Every law induced by (3)--(4) belongs to \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\), every null component has exactly constant CATE, and constants \(0<c_b<C_b<\infty\) depending only on the bumps and \(d\) satisfy
\[
 c_b\delta\leq D(P_1)\leq C_b\delta
 \tag{7}
\]
for every alternative component.  The null and alternative prior-predictive laws match for one observation conditional on all macro signs and also for observations in distinct active fine coordinates.  For observations \(1,2\) in the core of one fine cube and observation \(3\) in the core of a distinct fine cube of the same macro cube, define
\[
 \xi_i=s_e(A_i)B_i,; \upsilon_i=s_b(A_i,Y_i)B_i,;
 \kappa_i=\xi_i\upsilon_i,
 \]
where
\[
 s_e(a)=2(2a-1),;
 s_b(a,y)=\begin{cases}-8/5,&(a,y)=(0,0),\\ 8/3,&(a,y)=(0,1),\\ -2,&(a,y)=(1,0),\\ 2,&(a,y)=(1,1).
 \end{cases}
\]
The exact third canonical projection of the null-minus-alternative prior-predictive likelihood ratio is
\[
 \delta^2\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3,;
 \mathcal L_{12}
 =(\xi_1+\xi_2)(\upsilon_1+\upsilon_2)
 -(1+q_e^2\xi_1\xi_2)(\kappa_1+\kappa_2),
 \tag{8}
\]
and it is not identically zero.  Its contribution to the squared \(L^2(P_\star^{\otimes n})\) norm is at least
\[
 c_b(n)_3h^dH^d\delta^4.
 \tag{9}
\]
At \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), choose legal integer resolutions satisfying \(h\asymp\delta^5\), \(H\asymp\delta\), and put \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\) for fixed \(0<\epsilon\leq1\).  Then the terms \(n^2h\delta^4\), \(n^3hH\delta^4\), and \(n^4h^2H\delta^4\) are, respectively, \(o(1)\), \(\Theta(\epsilon^{10})=O(\epsilon^4)\), and \(o(1)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Because \(0\leq\vartheta\leq1\), every mass in (2) is nonnegative.  Their sum is one since \(\sum_{a,b}ab=0\).  Direct summation gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_0(\varepsilon_j\mid\sigma_Q)
 &=\frac14\sum_{a,b}a\{1+\vartheta\sigma_Qab\}=0,\\
 \mathbb E_0(\eta_j\mid\sigma_Q)
 &=\frac14\sum_{a,b}b\{1+\vartheta\sigma_Qab\}=0,\\
 \mathbb E_0(\varepsilon_j\eta_j\mid\sigma_Q)
 &=\frac14\sum_{a,b}ab\{1+\vartheta\sigma_Qab\}
 =\vartheta\sigma_Q.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{10}
\]
Under \(\mathbb P_1\), all three expectations are zero.  Since \(\varepsilon_j^2=\eta_j^2=1\), multiplication of (10) by \(q_e\), \(q_b\), and \(q_eq_b\), respectively, proves (6) and the asserted square identities.

We first verify the class conditions, rather than treating them as properties of the construction by definition.  The first inequality in (1), the first inequality in (5), and the triangle inequality show \([e_k]_{\alpha}\leq L\).  The corresponding bounds for \(v\) and \(G\), followed by the second inequality in (5), show \([m_{0,k}]_{\beta}\leq L\).  The second bound in (1) and the third inequality in (5) show \([\tau_1]_{\gamma}\leq L\); \(\tau_0\) has seminorm zero.  The analogous supremum bounds may be absorbed into the same fixed \(C_b\); because \(L\geq2\), they also give the required Hölder-ball supremum restrictions.  From \(|u|\leq q_e\), \(|v|\leq q_b\), and \(|G|\leq1\), the last two inequalities in (5) imply
\[
 \frac14\leq e_k\leq\frac34,;
 \frac14\leq m_{0,k}\leq\frac34,;
 \frac14\leq m_{0,k}+\tau_k\leq\frac34,; k\in\{0,1\}.
 \tag{11}
\]
For each displayed triple of regressions, take \(X\) exactly uniform on the full cube, draw \(A\mid X\) as Bernoulli with mean \(e_k(X)\), draw binary \(Y(0),Y(1)\) conditionally independently of \(A\) given \(X\) with means \(m_{0,k}(X)\) and \(m_{0,k}(X)+\tau_k(X)\), and set \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).  This constructs binary potential outcomes satisfying conditional exchangeability and consistency.  Equations (1), (5), and (11) verify every remaining defining condition of \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\).  In particular, this verification uses the original full-cube design and the original margins, and (3) gives \(\tau_0\equiv1/8\) component by component.

Let \(M=H^{-d}\) be the number of macro cubes, let \(g_Q\) be the rescaling of \(g\) to \(Q\), and write \(\mu_r=\int_{[0,1]^d}g(x)^r\,dx\).  Disjoint macro supports and a change of variables give
\[
 \int G^2\,d\lambda=\mu_2,;
 \int G\,d\lambda=H^d\mu_1\sum_Q\sigma_Q.
 \tag{12}
\]
Since \(H^dM=1\), the squared second expression is at most \(\mu_1^2\).  The fixed function \(g\) is nonconstant, so strict Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(\mu_2-\mu_1^2>0\).  From (4), (12), and the definition of \(D\),
\[
 4\delta(\mu_2-\mu_1^2)^{1/2}
 \leq D(P_1)\leq4\delta\mu_2^{1/2},
 \tag{13}
\]
which proves (7).  The stipulated bump properties are realizable: begin with a smooth macro collar bump, multiply its square root by a smooth finite square partition of unity on the fine lattice, and tensorize.  A smooth angle interpolation \((\cos\omega,\sin\omega)\) on each overlap has squared sum one, while fixed-width core subcubes give the stated lower-volume property.  Rescaling gives precisely (1), with a constant depending only on the fixed shapes and \(d\).

It remains to compute the predictive likelihood.  Relative to the interior reference law with conditional cell probabilities
\[
 (p^\star_{00},p^\star_{01},p^\star_{10},p^\star_{11})
 =\left(\frac5{16},\frac3{16},\frac14,\frac14\right),
 \tag{14}
\]
direct multiplication of the four Bernoulli cells gives, for arbitrary \(x\),
\[
 L_{0,i}=(1+s_e(A_i)u_i)(1+s_b(A_i,Y_i)v_i),
 \tag{15}
\]
and
\[
 L_{1,i}=(1+s_e(A_i)u_i)
 \{1+s_b(A_i,Y_i)v_i+s_e(A_i)s_b(A_i,Y_i)\delta\sigma_QG_Q(X_i)\}.
 \tag{16}
\]
For example, for \((A,Y)=(0,0)\), the ratio in (15) is \((1-2u)(1-8v/5)\), while the ratio in (16) is \((1-2u)\{1-8v/5+16\delta\sigma_QG_Q/5\}\); the other three rows give the displayed score table in the same way.  Thus (15)--(16) are exact identities, with no Taylor remainder.

Conditional on the macro signs, independence of the fine coefficient pairs and (6) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_0(u_iv_i\mid\sigma)=\delta\sigma_QG_Q(X_i),;
 \mathbb E_1(u_iv_i\mid\sigma)=0.
 \tag{17}
\]
All linear coefficient means vanish.  Expanding (15)--(16) and using (17) proves
\[
 \mathbb E_0(L_{0,i}\mid\sigma)
 =\mathbb E_1(L_{1,i}\mid\sigma)
 =1+s_e(A_i)s_b(A_i,Y_i)\delta\sigma_QG_Q(X_i).
 \tag{18}
\]
This proves exact one-observation matching.  When observations use disjoint active fine-coordinate sets, the relevant coefficient pairs are independent conditional on \(\sigma\); hence both joint predictive likelihoods are the product of the common factors (18).  This proves the distinct-fine-coordinate matching.

Now restrict observations \(1,2\) to the core of one fine coordinate and observation \(3\) to the core of a distinct coordinate in the same macro cube.  Put \(r=\delta\sigma_Q\).  On these cores, (15)--(16) reduce exactly to
\[
 L_{0,i}=(1+\xi_iU_j)(1+\upsilon_iV_j),
 \;
 L_{1,i}=(1+\xi_iU_j)(1+\upsilon_iV_j+\kappa_ir).
 \tag{19}
\]
For the shared coordinate of observations \(1,2\), the fixed squares and vanishing odd mixed moments in (10) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 N_{12}:=\mathbb E_0(L_{0,1}L_{0,2}\mid\sigma)
 ={}&1+\xi_1\xi_2q_e^2+\upsilon_1\upsilon_2q_b^2
 +(\xi_1+\xi_2)(\upsilon_1+\upsilon_2)r\\
 &+\xi_1\xi_2\upsilon_1\upsilon_2q_e^2q_b^2,
 \tag{20}\\
 A_{12}:=\mathbb E_1(L_{1,1}L_{1,2}\mid\sigma)
 ={}&(1+\xi_1\xi_2q_e^2)
 \{(1+\kappa_1r)(1+\kappa_2r)+\upsilon_1\upsilon_2q_b^2\}.
 \tag{21}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Consequently
\[
 N_{12}-A_{12}=r\mathcal L_{12}-r^2\mathcal Q_{12},;
 \mathcal Q_{12}=\kappa_1\kappa_2(1+q_e^2\xi_1\xi_2).
 \tag{22}
\]
Observation \(3\) has the common predictive factor \(1+\kappa_3r\) by (18).  Averaging (22), and then (22) times this factor, over the Rademacher sign gives
\[
 F_{12}=-\delta^2\mathcal Q_{12},;
 F_{123}=\delta^2(\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3-\mathcal Q_{12}).
 \tag{23}
\]
All one-coordinate differences and the two pairwise differences involving observation \(3\) vanish.  Möbius subtraction of these lower-coordinate marginals from \(F_{123}\) proves that the third canonical projection is exactly (8).

It is nonzero.  If all three binary rows equal \((1,1)\), then \(\xi_i=\upsilon_i=2B_i\), \(\kappa_i=4B_i^2\), and
\[
 \mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3
 =32B_1B_2B_3^2\{1-2q_e^2(B_1^2+B_2^2)\}.
 \tag{24}
\]
The last factor is at least \(3/4\) under \(q_e\leq1/4\).  The event in (24) has fixed positive probability under (14), and every selected core has volume at least \(c_bh^d\).  There are, up to constants depending only on \(d\),
\[
 H^{-d}(H/h)^d\{(H/h)^d-1\}\asymp H^dh^{-2d}
 \tag{25}
\]
ordered choices of a repeated fine coordinate and a distinct singleton coordinate in one macro cube.  Integrating the square of (8) on their cores and using (24)--(25) gives a one-triple squared norm at least \(c_bh^dH^d\delta^4\).  Canonical kernels on distinct sample-coordinate triples are orthogonal under the product reference law, because some coordinate occurs in only one triple and integration over that coordinate is zero.  Summing over triples proves (9).

Finally take \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\).  Integer meshes can be chosen within fixed factors of \(h=\delta^5\) and \(H=\delta\); by increasing those fixed factors if necessary, taking \(q_e=q_b=2\delta^{1/2}\), and then taking \(\epsilon\) sufficiently small, all inequalities in (5) hold for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Here \(\vartheta=1/4\), so all four conditional masses in (2) are strictly positive.  With \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\), direct substitution gives
\[
 n^2h\delta^4\asymp\epsilon^9n^{-7/10}=o(1),
 \;
 n^3hH\delta^4\asymp\epsilon^{10}=O(\epsilon^4),
 \;
 n^4h^2H\delta^4\asymp\epsilon^{15}n^{-1/2}=o(1).
 \tag{26}
\]
This proves every assertion.
added_lemmas.justification: This restores the load-bearing exact \(2+1\) likelihood calculation and evaluates it at the revised rough stress scale.
added_lemmas.gap: The projection is controlled at \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\); it does not control higher connected clusters.
added_lemmas.consumer: The repaired lower construction must include this mixed-occupancy term in its fixed-sample comparison.

added_lemmas.statement:
Under the hypotheses and notation of \(\texttt{lem:four-atom-cross-fine-third-projection}\), put observations \(1,2\) in the core of one fine cube and observations \(3,4,5\) in the cores of three mutually distinct fine cubes, all four fine cubes lying in the same macro cube.  The exact fifth canonical projection of the null-minus-alternative prior-predictive likelihood ratio is
\[
 \delta^4\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\kappa_4\kappa_5.
 \tag{27}
\]
It is not identically zero, and its contribution to the squared \(L^2(P_\star^{\otimes n})\) norm is at least
\[
 c_b(n)_5h^dH^{3d}\delta^8.
 \tag{28}
\]
At \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), \(h\asymp\delta^5\), \(H\asymp\delta\), and \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\) with fixed \(\epsilon>0\), the right side of (28) is of order \(\epsilon^{16}n^{1/5}\) and diverges.  Hence the four-atom construction cannot have a support-controlled squared-likelihood connected remainder of order \(O(\epsilon^4)\) at the proposed \(n^{-3/10}\) separation.  This conclusion concerns that \(L^2\) comparison; it does not by itself exclude a different prior or a direct Hellinger argument that does not pass through this divergent second likelihood moment.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For a set \(S\subseteq\{3,4,5\}\) of singleton observations, equation (22) in \(\texttt{lem:four-atom-cross-fine-third-projection}\) and conditional independence across the distinct fine coordinates give the exact null-minus-alternative marginal difference
\[
 F_{12,S}
 =\mathbb E_{\sigma_Q}\left[
 (r\mathcal L_{12}-r^2\mathcal Q_{12})
 \prod_{i\in S}(1+\kappa_ir)
 \right],; r=\delta\sigma_Q.
 \tag{29}
\]
Every marginal difference omitting observation \(1\) or \(2\) is zero by the conditional matching already proved.  Therefore the fifth canonical projection is the Möbius difference
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{S\subseteq\{3,4,5\}}(-1)^{3-|S|}F_{12,S}
 &=\mathbb E_{\sigma_Q}\left[
 (r\mathcal L_{12}-r^2\mathcal Q_{12})
 \prod_{i=3}^5\{(1+\kappa_ir)-1\}
 \right]\\
 &=\mathbb E_{\sigma_Q}\left[
 r^4\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\kappa_4\kappa_5
 -r^5\mathcal Q_{12}\kappa_3\kappa_4\kappa_5
 \right].
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{30}
\]
The macro sign is Rademacher, so \(\mathbb E r^4=\delta^4\) and \(\mathbb E r^5=0\).  Equation (30) is exactly (27).

To see that it is nonzero, take all five binary rows equal to \((1,1)\).  The calculation leading to (24) gives
\[
 \mathcal L_{12}=8B_1B_2\{1-2q_e^2(B_1^2+B_2^2)\},
 \; \kappa_i=4B_i^2.
 \tag{31}
\]
Under \(q_e\leq1/4\), the expression in braces is at least \(3/4\).  On the stipulated bump cores, (31) is bounded away from zero by a constant depending only on the fixed bump shapes.  The binary event in (31) has reference probability \(4^{-5}\).  For one ordered choice of four distinct fine cubes, integration over the five covariates contributes at least a constant times \(h^{5d}\).  The number of ordered choices in all macro cubes is
\[
 H^{-d}(H/h)^d\{(H/h)^d-1\}\{(H/h)^d-2\}\{(H/h)^d-3\}
 \asymp H^{3d}h^{-4d}.
 \tag{32}
\]
Multiplying (31)--(32) and squaring the coefficient \(\delta^4\) proves that the squared norm of this fifth canonical kernel is at least \(c_bh^dH^{3d}\delta^8\).

For the \(n\)-observation prior-predictive likelihood difference, canonical components indexed by different five-element subsets of sample coordinates are orthogonal under \(P_\star^{\otimes n}\): a coordinate in the symmetric difference appears in only one factor and that factor integrates to zero.  Hence the squared norm of the full likelihood difference is at least \(\binom n5\) times the preceding one-kernel norm.  Absorbing \(5!\) into \(c_b\) yields (28).

At the stated stress point,
\[
 (n)_5hH^3\delta^8\asymp n^5\delta^{16}
 =\epsilon^{16}n^{1/5}\longrightarrow\infty.
 \tag{33}
\]
Thus this exact connected component cannot be included in an \(O(\epsilon^4)\) squared-likelihood remainder uniformly in large \(n\).  Since a divergent chi-square contribution need not force the Hellinger distance to diverge without an additional likelihood-ratio integrability argument, the final qualification in the statement follows and avoids claiming more than (27)--(33) prove.
added_lemmas.justification: This computes the first connected cluster found beyond the controlled \(2+1\) term at the revised \(n^{-3/10}\) stress scale.
added_lemmas.gap: It rules out the proposed support-controlled squared-likelihood remainder for this prior but does not rule out a different prior or a direct Hellinger comparison.
added_lemmas.consumer: The open frontier target uses the lemma to specify exactly what a repaired converse must cancel or bypass.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: On the identical class \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\), define independently two finite, explicitly evaluable constructions.  The upper construction must select deterministic multiresolution tuning and produce one total data-driven test in \(\Phi_n\), with rejection probability at most \(a_0\) for every \(n\), worst-case type-II error at most \(b_0\) above a displayed upper-radius map, and certified arithmetic and memory costs in every dense and sparse occupancy regime.  The lower construction must consist of realizable full-cube binary laws in the same class, every component of each null prior must have exactly constant \(\tau\), and an original fixed-\(n\) likelihood, Hellinger, or total-variation calculation must give a displayed lower-radius map against all tests.  Neither repaired construction may be defined from the frozen quantities \(r_{\mathrm{test}}\) or \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}\), which remain regression diagnostics only.  Prove the corresponding upper and lower inequalities for \(\rho_n^*\), optimize both maps for every fixed \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L)\), including every equality-case logarithm, and prove that the independently obtained maps have the same order before introducing any common sharp-rate notation.  If they do not match, give the explicitly evaluable two-sided bracket and isolate the exact unmatched population-signal, stochastic-projection, or prior-predictive connected-cluster term.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The existing question requires equivalence of \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}\) and \(r_{\mathrm{test}}\), although the frozen theorems already show that neither handle can define the critical radius.  The replacement removes only that disproved route and preserves the maximal unchanged-class objective through independently derived lower and upper constructions.

proposed.statement: On the identical class \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\), define independently two finite, explicitly evaluable constructions.  The upper construction must select deterministic multiresolution tuning and produce one total data-driven test in \(\Phi_n\), with rejection probability at most \(a_0\) for every \(n\), worst-case type-II error at most \(b_0\) above a displayed upper-radius map, and certified arithmetic and memory costs in every dense and sparse occupancy regime.  The lower construction must consist of realizable full-cube binary laws in the same class, every component of each null prior must have exactly constant \(\tau\), and an original fixed-\(n\) likelihood, Hellinger, or total-variation calculation must give a displayed lower-radius map against all tests.  Neither repaired construction may be defined from the frozen quantities \(r_{\mathrm{test}}\) or \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}\), which remain regression diagnostics only.  Prove the corresponding upper and lower inequalities for \(\rho_n^*\), optimize both maps for every fixed \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L)\), including every equality-case logarithm, and prove that the independently obtained maps have the same order before introducing any common sharp-rate notation.  If they do not match, give the explicitly evaluable two-sided bracket and isolate the exact unmatched population-signal, stochastic-projection, or prior-predictive connected-cluster term.
proposed.justification: This remains the field-tier theorem target: a total uniformly calibrated test and an original fixed-\(n\), constant-null-supported converse must be proved on the identical class and optimized independently before any matching claim.
proposed.gap: At the revised stress separation, the exact \(2+1\) projection is controlled, but the same repeated fine-cell pair joined to three distinct fine-cell singletons has a fifth canonical projection whose squared \(L^2\) contribution grows as \(\epsilon^{16}n^{1/5}\).  A new cancellation or a direct Hellinger comparison, plus the matching upper concentration theorem and all-regime optimization, is still required.
proposed.consumer: A completed theorem would give causal-forest calibration and epidemiologic heterogeneity workflows a genuine detectability benchmark and an omnibus finite-sample procedure, without certifying any fitted forest or converting non-rejection into a homogeneity conclusion.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: Put \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\) and let \(b_n=n^{-2t/(4t+d)}\) for \(d\leq4t\), while \(b_n=n^{-4t/(4t+3d)}\) for \(d>4t\).  The proved all-regime statement is \(c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cb_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  On the proved no-penalty subregion \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\), \(\rho_n^*\asymp\rho_{n,e}^*\asymp n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\), with no logarithm at \(d=4\gamma\).  No independently derived repaired lower and upper maps have yet been proved equivalent.  The complete all-regime frontier, its unresolved transition logarithms, and the necessary direction of the known-propensity comparison therefore remain open; no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a pointwise CATE-estimation minimax rate in a larger model with a merely bounded covariate density and real outcomes; Section 3.1 supplies localized fuzzy-hypothesis and Hellinger machinery.  Its binary lower submodel uses a density uniform on an \(n\)-dependent support-with-holes \(S_{h,k}\), so that lower bound does not transfer downward to the present exact full-cube uniform-design subclass.
Theorems 4 and 6 give fixed-alternative consistency and a local weak limit for quantitative homogeneity tests over structured rule classes under the paper's nuisance conditions.

Theorems 1--2 establish asymptotic normality for propensity-reweighted pairwise and multisample adjusted \(U\)-statistics under consistent propensity estimation, independent stratum samples, stable positive sample fractions, and pointwise overlap.

Section 3 derives joint asymptotic normality and Gaussian-simulation calibration for multisample \(U\)-statistics testing equality of additive treatment effects across a fixed collection of mutually independent prespecified strata.

Theorem 6 gives asymptotic level, fixed-alternative consistency, and nontrivial \(n^{-1/2}\)-local power for a multiplier-bootstrap test of homogeneous restricted CATE with possibly right-censored duration outcomes.

Section 4 gives a conservative finite-sample-valid Fisher randomization test for the sharp null of one unknown constant individual treatment effect by maximizing randomization \(p\)-values over a confidence set for that nuisance effect.

The main martingale-transformation results give asymptotic level for a permutation test of a constant marginal-distribution shift with an estimated nuisance shift, retaining exact level only for the more restrictive sharp null.
Theorems 3 and 7 give asymptotic chi-square tests of equality of finitely many score-defined group average treatment effects under complete randomization, with sample splitting or cross-fitting.

Theorems 4.1 and 5.2 give matching nonasymptotic binned conditional-independence radii for fixed discrete responses and a continuous conditioner under total-variation smoothness, a different null manifold and separation metric from constant CATE.

Theorems 6 and 7 give null validity and spline minimax power for projected conditional covariance under common smoothness and nondegeneracy restrictions, rather than a fixed-sample three-smoothness CATE radius.

Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 characterize bias, variance, and optimal separate wavelet resolutions for estimation of a signed expected conditional covariance functional; they guide nuisance resolution but do not test an unknown constant CATE.
The main minimax theorems derive sharp heteroskedasticity-detection rates using a squared first-difference proxy under a rough unknown mean.
Theorem 1 gives asymptotic normality and type-I error control for an intra-fold split CATE-variance statistic under explicit nuisance learner-rate conditions.
The paper proves that the propensity score is ancillary for semiparametrically efficient estimation of the regular average treatment effect under ignorability.
Theorems 3.3 and 3.4 give asymptotic null validity and consistency against smooth local sieve alternatives for the null that the conditional average treatment effect is constant.

The paper develops \(L_1\)-type tests based on uniformly consistent nonparametric kernel estimators for conditional treatment-effect restrictions and proves asymptotically correct size, fixed-alternative consistency, and power against some local alternatives.
Section 1 records the classical nonadaptive Hölder goodness-of-fit boundary, and the paper establishes the iterated-logarithmic price of adaptation in wavelet testing.

open_obligations.obstruction: For the mandated four-atom law, the \(2+1\) contribution is only \(\Theta(\epsilon^{10})\) at \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\), but a repeated fine-cell pair together with three distinct fine-cell singletons in the same macro cube has exact fifth canonical projection \(\delta^4\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\kappa_4\kappa_5\).  Its squared \(L^2(P_\star^{\otimes n})\) contribution is at least \(c_b(n)_5h^dH^{3d}\delta^8\), which is \(c_b\epsilon^{16}n^{1/5}\) at \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), \(h\asymp\delta^5\), and \(H\asymp\delta\).  Therefore the proposed support-controlled chi-square connected remainder is not \(O(\epsilon^4)\).  This does not logically preclude a direct Hellinger comparison, but no such comparison follows from the frozen primitives or the computed likelihood projections.
open_obligations.attempted: The bounded four-atom probabilities, zero coordinate means, fixed squares, correlation shift, binary margins, Hölder bounds, exact uniform design, consistency, exchangeability, componentwise constant null CATE, alternative separation, one-observation matching, and distinct-fine matching were verified. prose_updates.tldr: The proved result remains an honest all-regime bracket for the fixed-sample observational critical radius, together with the known-propensity benchmark and a matched no-penalty subregion.  With \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), the radius lies between \(n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\) and the explicit single-scale rate \(n^{-2t/(4t+d)}\) for \(d\leq4t\), or \(n^{-4t/(4t+3d)}\) for \(d>4t\).  If \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\), both sides equal the known-propensity order.  The exact full-cube uniform design and fixed binary-regression margins are project-specific strengthenings; KBRW supplies only localized fuzzy-hypothesis methodology.  At the revised rough stress separation, the restored \(2+1\) projection is controlled, but an exact \(2+3\) fifth canonical projection has squared-likelihood scale \(\epsilon^{16}n^{1/5}\).  Thus this four-atom chi-square route fails, the complete frontier remains open, and no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

project_justification.gap: Existing homogeneity tests provide asymptotic validity, fixed-direction power, or finite-stratum comparisons, while existing minimax work concerns different null geometries, metrics, or pointwise CATE estimation.  On this project-specific binary exact-uniform class, the unresolved object is a matching fixed-sample lower and upper detection map across all three Hölder indices and all occupancy regimes.  The current likelihood audit shows that controlling the same-fine, \(2+1\), and nominal fourth-order terms does not control every higher connected macro--fine cluster.
project_justification.niche: The live mathematical niche is the likelihood-level interaction among an unknown constant-effect null, separate propensity and baseline roughness, macro-scale CATE variation, and repeated fine-cell collisions.  A sharp result must preserve exact uniform design, keep every null-prior component homogeneous, prove a direct finite-sample comparison, and pair it with an omnibus sparse-occupancy test on the identical class.
project_justification.fill: The established contribution supplies an explicit total single-scale fourth-order test, the all-regime bracket, the known-propensity benchmark, and a matched no-penalty subregion.  This round restores the exact \(2+1\) calculation, verifies it is only \(O(\epsilon^4)\) at \(n^{-3/10}\), and derives the previously uncharged \(2+3\) fifth canonical projection and its divergent squared-likelihood contribution.  That is a construction-specific diagnostic and a precise specification for the repaired converse, not a solution of the all-regime frontier.

prose_updates.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 is a method donor, not the source of the present exact class.  Its Theorem 1 permits a merely bounded covariate density and real outcomes, while its binary lower submodel is uniform on an \(n\)-dependent support-with-holes \(S_{h,k}\).  Because a converse on a larger class does not transfer downward to this exact full-cube uniform-design subclass, only the localized fuzzy-hypothesis and Hellinger architecture of Section 3.1 is imported here; the exact-uniform binary margins and every new likelihood calculation must be proved afresh.  NeykovBalakrishnanWasserman2021 gives collision-sensitive nonasymptotic conditional-independence tests under total-variation smoothness, but its null manifold and metric differ from unknown-constant CATE.  LundborgKimShahSamworth2024, corresponding to PCM arXiv:2211.02039, gives projected-conditional-covariance validity and spline power under its own common-smoothness and nondegeneracy conditions, not a uniform fixed-sample radius on this three-index causal class.  DukesStensrudBrioschiHudson2026, arXiv:2410.00985v4, studies structured-rule homogeneity through asymptotic size, fixed power, and local weak limits under supplied nuisance conditions.  McGrathMukherjee2026, arXiv:2212.14857v5, derives separate nuisance resolutions for estimating a signed expected conditional covariance, which informs tuning but does not solve constant-CATE testing.  KBRW's pointwise estimation elbow, NBW's conditional-independence radius, PCM's projection test, Dukes et al.'s rule-class procedure, and McGrath--Mukherjee's estimation functional therefore do not supply the missing identical-class converse or omnibus test.  The remaining direct CATE-homogeneity predecessors in the comparator table are asymptotic, finite-stratum, score-group, distribution-shift, or sharp unit-level procedures; none provides the requested all-regime fixed-sample minimax frontier.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The frozen mixture envelope is invalid as a universal converse handle, and the frozen testing envelope is not sharp; both remain regression diagnostics.  For the bounded nested four-atom repair, every null component has constant CATE and all class-side and one-observation checks hold.  At \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), \(h\asymp\delta^5\), \(H\asymp\delta\), and \(\delta=\epsilon n^{-3/10}\), the restored \(2+1\) contribution is \(\Theta(\epsilon^{10})\), hence controlled.  However, the exact \(2+3\) fifth canonical projection is \(\delta^4\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\kappa_4\kappa_5\), and its squared-likelihood contribution is at least \(c_b(n)_5hH^3\delta^8\asymp c_b\epsilon^{16}n^{1/5}\).  This disproves an \(O(\epsilon^4)\) support-controlled chi-square remainder for that prior.  Chi-square divergence alone does not exclude a direct Hellinger bound, so a different prior, a further cancellation, or a genuinely direct Hellinger comparison is still needed, as are the upper alternative dichotomy and sparse-occupancy concentration theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal estimand remains the centered \(L^2\) norm of the CATE, and the statistical class remains the original project-specific binary exact-full-cube-uniform Hölder class with fixed overlap and interior margins.  The known-propensity rate is a comparator and carries no novelty claim.  The proved observational content is the all-regime bracket and the sufficient no-penalty region; smoothness adaptation is not claimed.  The restored \(2+1\) and new \(2+3\) calculations diagnose one prescribed four-atom prior and do not prove that every null-supported prior pays the same term.  KBRW is used only for methodological architecture, and its larger-model lower bound is not asserted on this subclass.  The complete rough-nuisance frontier, transition logarithms outside the proved region, and the necessary-and-sufficient propensity-value frontier remain open.  No conclusion certifies a fitted forest, and non-rejection is not evidence that the CATE is constant.
